summary.headline: Syrma SGS Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 73% YoY to about INR2,000 crores; FY27 growth guidance raised to 40-45%, implying about INR7,000 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was about INR2,000 crores (up 73% YoY, 25% QoQ), with H1 at INR3,603 crores (up 71%). H1 EBITDA was INR355 crores at a 9.9% margin, and H1 PAT was INR230 crores (up 98%). Operating cash flow turned positive in Q2 at about INR120 crores, and net working capital fell to 63 days from 71 days in Q1. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 40-45% but kept FY27 EBITDA margin guidance at 10-10.5%, citing supply-chain constraints and front-loaded orders.

financial_highlights.value: INR258 crores; treasury about INR1,000 crores; gross debt INR746 crores
approx. INR200 crores, of which about INR140 crores for PCB project

financial_highlights.change: Auto ~30%; consumer and industrial ~24.5-25% each; healthcare 8%; IT and railways ~12%

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Revenue up 91% YoY in Q2, about 26% of operating revenue; management said H1 automotive grew over 80%.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: About 29% of Q2 operating revenue; H1 consumer revenue about INR1,100 crores+, front-loaded and expected to taper in H2.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue up 86% YoY and 31% QoQ in Q2; management expects faster growth in H2.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Grew 61% YoY; described as a good-margin business contributing about 8% of order book.

segments.name: IT and railways
segments.commentary: Revenue up 69% YoY and 82% QoQ; about 14% of Q2 operating revenue. IT is low-margin (memory modules, gaming laptop assemblies); railways is high-margin.

segments.name: Elcome and Syrma Johari (SJML)
segments.commentary: Elcome contributed about INR135 crores and SJML about INR140 crores in H1; FY27 targets INR300-350 crores (Elcome) and about INR300 crores (SJML).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth raised to 40-45% (about INR7,000 crores); management said it could reach INR7,000-7,500 crores depending on supply chain, and later stated 45%+ growth.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 10-10.5%; H1 margin was just under 10%.
FY28 revenue expected to cross USD 1 billion; FY27-FY28 expected growth of 30-35% for the next 3-5 years.
FY27 export revenue expected above INR1,700 crores (FY26 base INR1,200 crores); FY28 exports targeted around INR2,000 crores.
FY28 EBITDA margin expected at 10.5-11% or marginally above 11%, aided by margin-accretive projects.
Supply-chain constraints expected for 5-6 months (management also cited 6-9 months), easing around April-June 2027 / Q1 FY28.
Working capital expected at 60-65 days on an annualised basis; management said sub-60 days is unlikely in the next 6 months.

Capex: PCB project about INR800-900 crores total (about INR400-450 crores by March 2027 and a similar amount in FY28); other greenfield and brownfield capex INR100-150 crores per year for the next 2 years.
capex_capacity: PCB project: power-on targeted by March 2027, trial production March-April 2027, commercial production targeted April 2027 and series production June-September 2027. Expected to yield INR200-250 crores (FY28, about 6-7 months) and INR900-1,000 crores (FY29, 70-80% utilisation) on about INR800-900 crores of investment; management also cited up to INR1,200-1,350 crores at full ramp.
PCB steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 15-18% excluding PLI; management said FY28 PAT loss is not expected even though utilisation may be about 40% in the initial year.
CCL (copper clad laminate) plant planned after PCB stabilises; execution to start in Q3-Q4 FY28, ready around December 2028.
Elemaster JV factory commissioned in early September 2026; regulatory approvals (ISO, IRIS, RDSO) expected in FY27; FY28 revenue INR150-200 crores. Elemaster capex about INR40-50 crores.
Camera module capex about INR25-30 crores initially; automotive focus with revenue of INR50-100 crores to start. Kaga JV capex INR30-50 crores max; FY28 revenue INR100-150 crores.

ECMS applications for 5-6 projects, including PCB, CCL, HDI/flex, camera modules and a small magnetics project. ISM participation is under discussion with a credible partner; an announcement is hoped for within about 6 months.
ARC system deployed in 3-4 plants: 5-6% OEE improvement on SMT lines; target 6-10% across all plants.
demand_pricing: Demand described as strong across verticals; H1 growth by vertical: automotive 80%+, healthcare 78%, industrial 58%, IT 100%+ (small base), railways 45%, consumer 62%.

Pricing: cost push about 5%; material cost up about 3% in Q2; roughly INR50-70 crores of the Q2 revenue attributed to pass-through cost push. Pass-through exists with customers, but no value add on cost push, which dilutes margin percentage.
Exports are fixed-price contracts; natural hedge against imports. A pass-through forex mechanism applies to most large domestic businesses.

Framework agreement (about USD 250 million per annual report) with a global customer in industrial, power management, power distribution and data center; NPIs done and ramp plan agreed; annualised revenue at least INR500-1,500 crores, with full impact from FY28. Management said it is not a one-off contract.
Order book growth lagged revenue growth; INR1,200 crores of the INR7,420 crores order book is beyond 12 months, as auto customers now place longer-dated orders due to supply constraints.
Customer concentration: top customer about 12-14% of revenue; top 5 about 38%, top 10 about 50%, top 20 about 66% (H1). Exports about 26% of revenue.
Onboarded about 32 customers in FY26 and about 18 in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is ODM expanding beyond healthcare/medtech, and what products are being developed; how to reconcile full-year guidance implying a slower H2 given H2 is seasonally stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: ODM is growing in medtech, defence, RFID and other areas, with industrial ODM products being developed; ODM mainly in healthcare, defence, power electronics, RFID and magnetics over 2-3 years. Management said H2 guidance is conservative due to supply-chain concerns, not demand; guidance raised to 40-45% growth, roughly INR7,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why does full-year guidance imply a sharp H2 slowdown after Q2 at about INR2,000 crores, and what drives the front-loading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 was boosted by front-loaded customer orders and consumer segment (INR1,100 crores+ in H1) is expected to taper. Final outcome of INR7,000 to 7,500 crores depends on supply chain. Q1 revenue was about INR2,600 crores per the analyst's calculation, not disputed.

qa_highlights.question: Details, timelines and size of the USD 250 million framework agreement; is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPIs and early production runs are done and a ramp-up plan is agreed; full impact from FY28, not a one-off. Annualised revenue estimated at least INR500-1,500 crores, with sectors being industrial, power management, power distribution and data center.

qa_highlights.question: What share of growth is organic from new customers versus pricing, and how ready is the platform for USD 1 billion in FY28 (hiring, capex)?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth by vertical: automotive 80%+, healthcare 78%, industrial 58%, IT 100%+, railways 45%, consumer 62%. Cost push about 5%; roughly INR50-70 crores of Q2 revenue attributed to pass-through. Management said no major capex needed for the base business; the heavy lifting is processes and program management.

qa_highlights.question: PCB project revenue, investment, margins and PLI/capital subsidy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 PCB revenue about INR200-250 crores (6-7 months); FY29 about INR900-1,000 crores at 70-80% utilisation on about INR800-900 crores investment. Steady-state EBITDA 15-18% excluding PLI. Capital subsidy of about INR200 crores expected after claims filed by March 2028; PLI realisation with a 6-12 month lag.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build, working capital and whether customers are stockpiling?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose from about INR1,000 crores (March 2026) to INR1,570 crores but stayed at about 71 days; working capital 63 days. Management guided 60-65 days annualised and said sub-60 days is unlikely in the next 6 months. Strategic stock held in critical components until supply eases.

risks_watch: Supply-chain constraints: management expects 5-6 months (also cited 6-9 months), easing around April-June 2027; lead times for active components up to 36 weeks and passives up to 16 weeks. Guidance depends on this.
Margin dilution: pass-through of cost push (about 5%) carries no value add, diluting EBITDA margin percentage. H1 EBITDA margin 9.9%; FY27 guided at 10-10.5%.
PCB execution: power-on by March 2027, commercial production April 2027, series production June-September 2027; PCB steady-state margin 15-18% excluding PLI; initial year utilisation around 40%.
Working capital and inventory: about INR1,570 crores inventory; INR1,200 crores of the INR7,420 crores order book beyond 12 months; sub-60 days not expected in the next 6 months.
Customer concentration: top customer 12-14% of revenue; top 5 about 38%, top 10 about 50%; consumer segment front-loaded and expected to taper in H2.
Elemaster JV (regulatory approvals ISO, IRIS, RDSO expected in FY27) and Kaga JV (IATF 16949 needed) timing; ISM participation not yet concrete, with an announcement hoped within about 6 months.
key_quotes: Demand side, we are very, very bullish.
The supply chain is still an area of concern.
We have pass-through mechanisms with all customers, but we don't get a value-add on the cost push and that results in slight dilution in the margin profile.
It's not a one-off contract for this.
We remain mindful of the importance of margin discipline, working capital management, cash conversion cycle, capital efficiency as the business grows.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and long-term growth, but deliberately cautious on FY27 guidance, which management attributes to supply-chain constraints and front-loaded orders rather than demand. Management was candid about margin dilution from pass-through cost push and about inventory held as strategic stock.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth raised to 40-45% (~INR7,000 cr), backed by open order book of INR7,420 cr (INR1,200 cr beyond 12 months), strong demand (H1 +71%) and Elemaster JV commissioned, but PCB capacity only comes live around April 2027 and supply-chain constraints persist for 5-6 months; FY27 EBITDA margin guided 10-10.5%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY28 EBITDA margin is guided at 10.5-11% from margin-accretive projects such as PCB (15-18% steady-state ex-PLI), but FY27 is guided flat at 10-10.5% and cost pass-through of about 5% dilutes the percentage.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: PCB project (INR800-900 cr) targets commercial production April 2027 and series production June-September 2027, with INR140 cr of Q2 capex already spent; Elemaster JV factory already commissioned in early September 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue up 71% with exports up 80% and ODM up 117%, the open order book is INR7,420 cr, and FY28 revenue is expected to cross USD 1 billion, though H2 consumer volumes are expected to taper.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: PCB capex of INR400-450 cr due by March 2027 plus a similar amount in FY28 is already committed, and the CCL plant, camera module and Kaga JV are planned next, with no utilisation-driven trigger needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management raised FY27 growth to 40-45% and later said 45%+, with a INR7,420 cr order book and H1 revenue up 71%, but it frames H2 as conservative because of supply constraints.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 10-10.5% against H1 at 9.9%, and supply-chain constraints for 5-6 months could cap the INR7,000 cr revenue target if the INR7,000-7,500 cr range is missed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PCB commercial production in April 2027, camera modules (INR50-100 cr revenue to start), Kaga JV (FY28 revenue INR100-150 cr) and ODM products in defence, RFID and industrial, all guided with a plan behind them.

rows.label: USD 250m framework agreement with global customer
rows.why: NPIs done and ramp plan agreed, with annualised revenue of at least INR500-1,500 cr and full impact from FY28.

rows.label: Working capital cycle 60-65 days
rows.why: NWC fell from 71 days in Q1 to 63 days in Sep-26 and management guided 60-65 days annualised, though sub-60 is unlikely in the next 6 months.

rows.label: ISM / ECMS incentive announcement
rows.why: ECMS applications for 5-6 projects are filed and ISM participation is under discussion with a partner, but it is not yet concrete.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the USD 1 billion FY28 ambition and the framework agreement, but cautious on FY27 guidance and candid about margin dilution from pass-through cost push and strategic inventory; analysts pressed on the implied H2 slowdown, Q1 revenue and the inventory build.
